title: South African real retail demand grows with category-specific food, clothing, and general-dealer contribution
source_unit: Statistics South Africa P6242.1 Retail Trade Sales, July 2026

denominator.unit: aggregate South African retail trade sales at constant 2019 prices; not household respondents

real_retail_sales_annual_change.unit: percent from July 2025 at constant 2019 prices

three_month_annual_change.unit: percent for the three months ended July 2026 versus the three months ended July 2025

three_month_seasonally_adjusted_change.unit: percent versus the preceding three months

observations.method: Statistics South Africa retail trade sales release using constant-2019-price and seasonally adjusted retail-sales estimates; the release reports monthly, three-month, and year-over-year comparisons.
observations.uncertainty: This is an establishment-based aggregate series, not household-level real consumption or welfare. Category movements can reflect prices, stock, population, timing, and retailer composition; the public key-finding page does not provide household denominators or individual trajectories.
observations.subgroup: South African retail establishments and industry categories; no household-income, age, place, or consumer subgroup in the key findings.
observations.counterinterpretation: Positive real retail growth can coexist with unequal access, debt stress, food insecurity, or reduced cultural spending; aggregate sales do not show who purchased or whether quantity, quality, or substitution changed.

observations.period: July 2026; category contributions to real annual growth

denominator.unit: aggregate South African retail trade category index; contributions are percentage points to total real annual change

general_dealers_change.unit: percent year over year; contribution 1.3 percentage points

other_retailers_change.unit: percent year over year; contribution 0.8 percentage points

textiles_clothing_footwear_leather_chang.unit: percent year over year; contribution 0.5 percentage points

specialized_food_beverage_tobacco_change.unit: percent year over year; contribution 0.4 percentage points

observations.method: Statistics South Africa category-level decomposition of the July 2026 real retail-trade movement; percentage-point contributions are reported by the statistical release.
observations.uncertainty: Category contributions are not household budget shares and do not reveal whether growth reflects more units, different product mix, or price deflation. ‘Other retailers’ is broad and not a cultural-consumption category.
observations.subgroup: Retail industry categories in South Africa.
observations.counterinterpretation: Clothing and food growth may reflect essential replacement, seasonal demand, or distribution changes rather than discretionary consumer confidence; general-dealer growth does not identify lower- or higher-income consumers.

related_sources.claim: Statistics South Africa archive identifies the July 2026 release as the latest P6242.1 publication and provides access to prior releases.
Official P6242.1 publication format and constant-2019-price retail category tables provide methodological context for the series.

boundary: This record adds a South African real retail and category-demand layer to the Japan household contraction, Great Britain channel shift, and U.S. aggregate-spending records. It does not measure household welfare, online behavior, cultural attendance, inequality of access, or causal category demand.
